```java
return Biweekly.write(ical).go();
```
```java
ical.setExperimentalProperty("X-WR-TIMEZONE", TimeZone.getDefault().getID());
```
```java
ical.setMethod(new Method("PUBLISH"));
```

The bug occurs because the exported dates default to UTC when using `Biweekly.write(ical).go()`, which does not account for the local timezone settings. The `X-WR-TIMEZONE` property is set to the local timezone, but it is not effectively applied during the export process, leading to incorrect date representations, especially during daylight savings time changes.

```java
StringWriter ret = new StringWriter();
```
```java
ICalWriter writer = new ICalWriter(ret, ICalVersion.V2_0);
```
```java
writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault());
```
Reason:

This ensures that the exported dates are correctly represented in the local timezone, thus resolving the issues caused by daylight savings time changes.
